key_insight: RARL couples reinforcement learning with local reachability maps and Lambert reconstruction so the policy learns intermediate waypoint selection for feasible multi-impulse interplanetary transfers.
engineering_relevance: The approach offers a reusable trajectory-design interface that improves policy reuse across varying departure states while preserving near-reference maneuver quality for Earth–Mars transfers.
method: Compute first-order local reachability sets from bounded velocity perturbations to define reachable next-node positions.
Let the policy choose a waypoint inside this ellipsoidal set, then use Lambert reconstruction to generate the maneuver on a dynamically consistent ballistic arc.
Finish with a terminal two-impulse rendezvous and use a linear maneuver-demand metric for reward shaping.
evidence_signal: On a two-body Earth–Mars benchmark, three training runs achieved a mean cost of 10.23 km/s (1.72% above a local sequential convex programming reference), and multi-state policies completed all 10,000 held-out Monte Carlo departures without impulse-cap violations.
watch_item: The method depends on accurate local reachability approximations and classical astrodynamics assumptions, so performance may degrade when dynamics are strongly nonlinear or model mismatch is significant.
paper_title: Reachability-Informed Reinforcement Learning for Multi-Impulse Interplanetary Transfers
